technology.value: In-ice radio antenna stations: each with three strings of antennas ~100 m deep in the firn plus surface antennas, detecting the Askaryan radio pulse from neutrino-induced showers in ice
technology.quote: Each station is composed of 24 low-noise receiving antennas installed in a hybrid configuration with both near-surface and deep receivers. ... The deep antennas are deployed in three boreholes down to 100 meters depth.

intervals.label: first 7 stations built
intervals.quote: with 7 stations deployed during the first two boreal summer field seasons of 2021 and 2022

intervals.label: deployment paused
intervals.quote: RNO-G paused deployment in 2023 in order to evaluate the instrument performance and design aspects before pushing forward to complete the array.

station_count.quote: 7 stations deployed during the first two boreal summer field seasons of 2021 and 2022

depth_max.quote: The deep antennas are deployed in three boreholes down to 100 meters depth.

description.value: Three boreholes per station (a power string carrying the phased-array trigger antennas, plus two helper strings), holding 15 receiving antennas in total, down to ~100 m below the surface
description.quote: 15 total Rx. antennas & 2 Tx. calibration pulser antennas installed in 3 boreholes ... The deep antennas are deployed in three boreholes down to 100 meters depth.
description.note: 15 is the station total across the three boreholes (24 receiving antennas per station minus 9 near-surface), not 15 per string; the Summit Station project page's wording 'three strings of 15 antennas' is ambiguous.

description.quote: The LPDAs are installed in trenches just below the snow surface in three separate rows that are centered on each borehole radial axis. Each row of LPDAs consists of three LPDAs
description.note: 9 = three trenches (one per borehole) of three log-periodic dipole antennas (LPDAs) each, as stated in the quoted passage; the paper also refers to 'the nine surface channels'.

summary.plain: Stations of buried and surface radio antennas, spaced more than a kilometre apart on the Greenland ice sheet, listening for the radio crackle of the highest-energy neutrinos.
summary.technical: RNO-G station design: three boreholes (~100 m depth) holding 15 receiving antennas in total plus 9 near-surface antennas (24 receiving channels) per station, on a 1.25 km grid; 7 stations built over the 2021-2022 field seasons, deployment paused in 2023 pending a performance/design review.
